Read and write a dichotomous key stored in SDD

Source: R/sdd.R
readSDDKey.Rd

Besides character matrices, an SDD file can hold ready-made identification keys (<IdentificationKey> elements): a tree of leads, each with a statement and either further leads, a taxon or a pointer to another key in the file. readSDDKey() reads one into a dimoose key, writeSDDKey() stores a dimoose key that way. Lucid's pathway-key builder exports this form.

Usage

readSDDKey(file, key = 1, desc = NULL, dataset = NULL)

writeSDDKey(key, file, title = NULL, lang = "en")

Arguments

file

Path of the SDD file.

key

For readSDDKey(), which key of the file to read: its position or its id. For writeSDDKey(), the dimoose key to write.

desc

Title of the key; by default the key's label in the file.

dataset

Which <Dataset> of the file to read, by position; by default the first one that holds a key.

title

Title of the SDD dataset; by default the key's description.

lang

Language of the text, as an xml:lang code.

Value

readSDDKey() returns a dimoose key; writeSDDKey() returns file, invisibly.

Details

In SDD the leads form a tree (each lead names its parent lead) and are not numbered. On reading, the leads that share a parent become a couplet and the couplets are numbered in the usual order of a printed key (the first lead of couplet 1 goes to couplet 2, and so on). A lead that points to another key of the same file (<Subkey>) continues with that key's first couplet, so a key split over several SDD keys comes back as one. A question on a lead (or on the key itself) becomes the Question of the couplet it leads to. A lead that ends without a taxon is kept, and reported by key$validate().

On writing, a couplet that is reached from more than one lead (a reticulate key) is written out once under each of them, because an SDD lead can have only one parent. Images and links attached to leads or taxa (Image, TaxonUrl) and other extra columns of the key are not written.

See also

readSDD() for the character matrix of an SDD file, readLucidKey() for Lucid's own pathway-key formats.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "insects-key.sdd.xml", package = "dimoose")
k <- readSDDKey(f)
k
#> <dimoose key> Key to some orders of insects
#>   4 couplets, 8 leads, 5 taxa, up to 3 steps deep (2.4 on average)
k$leads[, c("Statement", "Choice", "Character", "Next", "Taxon")]
#>   Statement Choice                                                  Character
#> 1         1      a                                               Wings absent
#> 2         1      b                                              Wings present
#> 3         2      a     Body flattened from side to side, 1-2 mm long; jumping
#> 4         2      b Body flattened from above, 10-15 mm long, with three tails
#> 5         3      a                                       Forewings membranous
#> 6         3      b         Forewings hard covers that meet in a straight line
#> 7         4      a                           Hindwings reduced to small knobs
#> 8         4      b      Hindwings present; wings and body covered with scales
#>   Next        Taxon
#> 1    2             
#> 2    3             
#> 3    - Siphonaptera
#> 4    -    Zygentoma
#> 5    4             
#> 6    -   Coleoptera
#> 7    -      Diptera
#> 8    -  Lepidoptera

out <- writeSDDKey(sharkKey(), tempfile(fileext = ".xml"))
readSDDKey(out)
#> <dimoose key> Key to the families of sharks in the Western Central Pacific.
#>   23 couplets, 46 leads, 24 taxa, up to 12 steps deep (7.5 on average)
